paper.title_en: Observation of Crossover from Repulsive to Attractive Interactions between Two $nS$-Rydberg Atoms in Dual-Species Atom Arrays
paper.abstract_en: Dual-species Rydberg atom arrays provide a flexible platform for engineering long-range interactions beyond the conventional isotropic blockade regime. We spectroscopically study interactions between different $s$-state Rydberg levels in a $^{87}\mathrm{Rb}$--$^{85}\mathrm{Rb}$ optical-tweezer array. By varying the principal-quantum-number difference $Δn$ around $61S_{1/2}$, we observe a crossover from repulsive to attractive interactions. We identify a distinct regime at $Δn=2$ in which Förster-enhanced electronic spin exchange dominates over orbital exchange and produces a strongly bond-orientation-dependent pair spectrum. Time-domain collective-excitation measurements reveal this geometry-dependent spin exchange through a pronounced anisotropy of the double-excitation probability. For $Δn=1$, by contrast, orbital exchange dominates and the interaction is nearly isotropic. These results establish the principal-quantum-number difference and bond orientation as complementary control parameters for tailoring Rydberg interaction spectra and collective excitation dynamics, opening new opportunities for engineering spin-dependent Hamiltonians in programmable atom arrays.
